topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecture and outlines its learning aims.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the mechanisms, clinical uses, and toxic limitations of standard physical and cytotoxic cancer treatments.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cellular defects and vulnerabilities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies designed to selectively eliminate cancer cells by targeting specific hormone dependencies, checkpoint losses, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitors and mechanisms of targeted therapy resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how small-molecule inhibitors exploit oncogene addiction in hyperactivated kinases and detail how cancer cells evolve resistance and drug addiction.

topics.label: Antibody-based targeted therapeutics
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates deliver targeted cytotoxicity against cancer surface antigens.

topics.label: Tumor immunology and modern immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence for immune surveillance and the mechanisms of modern immune checkpoint, bispecific, and CAR T-cell therapies.

topics.label: Global challenges, historical progress, and future considerations in oncology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate broader historical trends, genomic stratification challenges, and ethical dilemmas shaping the future of cancer care.
